liz: Quick heads-up — bringing up tempest-embed-v2 (quant int4) on the multilingual holdout and seeing a surprising drop in recall@1 compared to fp16 :eyes:

sam: Which eval and numbers? can you paste the exact output?

liz: Eval command: `./tools/eval/recall.py --model tempest-embed-v2 --quant int4 --holdout ml20k --batch 32`

liz: Output (sample summary):
```
recall@1: 0.842
recall@5: 0.952
recall@1_fp16: 0.884
recall@5_fp16: 0.957
delta_r1: -0.042
```

kevin: Oof, -4.2% at R@1 is sizable. Is this uniform across langs?

liz: Not uniform — most of the drop concentrated in zh/ja/ko. en/fr nearly unchanged.

anjali: Can you paste per-lang breakdown?

liz: zh: int4 r1 0.72 vs fp16 0.84; ja: 0.69 vs 0.83; ko: 0.75 vs 0.86; en: 0.89 vs 0.90

sam: That pattern screams tokenizer/subword distribution + quantization clipping in low-frequency subspaces.

kevin: Two quick hypotheses: per-tensor quant scale hurting rare-token dims OR whitening amplification (we do PCA->whiten->L2).

anjali: Try rerun with `--perchannel-quant` and `--skip-whitening` (two separate runs) on a 2k subset.

liz: Starting both now on a small sample (2k). `--perchannel-quant` job queued.

ci-bot: job 45872 queued, running on g4dn.xlarge

ci-bot: job 45873 queued, running on g4dn.xlarge

layover: ETA ~12m for the first results

kevin: Also check embedding norm distributions: `np.percentile(norms, [1,10,50,90,99])` for int4 vs fp16. quant can compress tails.

eva: I pushed a quick viz for cluster drift — https://internal.redwood.ai/embeddings/viz/4955 (UMAP colored by lang + R@1 drop per point)

liz: thx — UMAP shows clusters for zh/jp spread wider after int4, looks like small rotations.

sam: If per-channel fixes it, we can ship per-channel quant for those model sizes. If skip-whitening helps, maybe we need to retrain PCA on quantized embeddings (or run post-quant recalibration).

anjali: Action items: 1) liz to attach per-lang percentiles + norms, 2) run per-channel & skip-whitening, 3) if fixed, create canary with per-channel for non-en langs.

liz: Will post numbers + raw eval logs when both jobs finish.

kevin: Also throw in an INT8 run for comparison (might be closer to fp16).

liz: good call — adding INT8 quick run to the queue.

ci-bot: job 45874 queued, running on g4dn.2xlarge

sam: If nothing helps, we may need small recalibration dataset (5k multilang) to re-learn PCA/whiten on quantized embeddings.

anjali: Agreed. Keep the thread updated. Thanks team :thumbsup:
